portfolio.title: Healthcare Insights: What Our Data Tells Us About Hospital Procedures and Patient Care
portfolio.description: This project explores the hidden narratives within healthcare data, inspired by a personal experience in the emergency room. Motivated by a strong interest in healthcare analytics, the project aims to uncover patterns in hospital stays, procedures, and medication use to improve patient care. Readers will gain insights into how data analysis can inform healthcare decisions and policies. Key findings include the prevalence of cardiovascular-related specialties, the correlation between procedure count and hospital stay duration, the non-impact of race on procedure frequency, and the widespread use of insulin across all age groups.

portfolio.title: Courtside Views: 2022 NBA Season Visualized in Tableau
portfolio.description: This was an analysis I did of 2022 NBA Basketball Stats. I looked at the frequency of 3-pointers made per position for every team, key statistics like total points, assists and rebounds per player. One key finding was that James Harden made the most assists as a point guard with 1,334. A positive relationship was found between the number of assists and the total points earned. This means the more assists you get the more points you get. This is just some of the key findings, check out the full project below!

portfolio.title: Mine & Refine: Python's Journey into Data Depths
portfolio.description: In this project, I share my journey of applying Python to a real-world data analysis project involving mining operations—a field I had no prior experience in. Driven by a desire to sharpen my skills, I explored a dataset spanning March to September 2017 to uncover what happened on June 1st. Despite not finding strong correlations between key variables, I discovered unexpected trends, like a midday dip in iron concentrate alongside a spike in silica, and a pH drop linked to changes in equipment levels. This project not only deepened my understanding of data analysis but also reinforced how much insight can be drawn from asking the right questions and diving into the details.

portfolio.title: Mapping Money: What World Bank Loans Reveal About Countries in Need
portfolio.description: In this project, I dive into a global dataset from the World Bank to uncover what loan data reveals about countries in need—and some that have paid back more than they owe. This project was my opportunity to sharpen my SQL skills while exploring real-world financial patterns. As I analyzed the data, I uncovered stories behind the numbers, from India’s massive loan count to Mozambique’s unexpected overpayments. What started as a technical challenge quickly became a deeper exploration of economic dynamics and global aid. Through this article, I hope to show how even complex financial data can tell compelling stories when viewed through the right lens.

portfolio.title: Understanding Profit and Delivery Challenges in Supply Chains with PowerBI
portfolio.description: In this project, I set out to explore what really impacts supply chain efficiency, inspired by a documentary that highlighted how shipping delays can ripple through entire businesses. Using data from Sword Consulting Group and analyzing it with PowerBI, I discovered some surprising patterns—like the fact that while customers spend the most on computers and electronics, it’s actually fishing products that come with higher price tags despite lower purchase volume. Even more unexpected was that neither price nor product category seemed to influence shipping speed. This project not only deepened my understanding of data-driven supply chain analysis but also showed how valuable insights can emerge from everyday business data.

portfolio.title: Behind the Bell: Insights into Massachusetts Schools
portfolio.description: In this project, I analyzed data from 1,861 schools across the Massachusetts Education System, covering nearly one million students, to uncover trends in graduation rates, college attendance, and academic performance. One of the most interesting findings was the positive correlation between average class size and college attendance—suggesting that slightly larger classes (particularly in the 10–20 range) may be linked to higher college-going rates. Surprisingly, there was no clear relationship between economic disadvantage and college attendance. I also looked at 4th grade math scores and found that more schools fell below the passing threshold than above it, raising important questions about what sets the higher-performing schools apart and how struggling schools can improve.

portfolio.title: Uncovering the Secrets of Food Delivery Success
portfolio.description: In this project, I took my love for food delivery and turned it into a data-driven investigation into customer behavior and marketing effectiveness. What started as a curiosity about why people choose certain services quickly evolved into a deeper dive into who spends the most, which campaigns actually work, and what patterns emerge across income and age groups. Using real-world data, I found that while Campaign 6 drove the most sign-ups, it didn’t lead to higher spending—something I didn’t expect. I also discovered that people aged 36 to 65 are the biggest spenders, and income does influence delivery habits, though most customers fall within a surprisingly moderate spending range. This project gave me new perspective on an everyday service I already enjoy, showing how even our meal choices can tell meaningful stories through data.

portfolio.title: R You Ready? Cracking the Code of Employee Attrition
portfolio.description: In this project, I set out to explore the reasons why employees leave their jobs, using IBM’s HR data to test common assumptions—like the belief that age plays a major role in retention. What I found challenged that idea and gave me a deeper appreciation for how complex employee behavior really is. With a background in psychology, I was especially drawn to the human side of the data, and this analysis gave me the perfect opportunity to blend that interest with business insight. My findings revealed that while age has little correlation with income or attrition, younger employees do tend to leave more often, and total working years are actually a much stronger predictor of income than age. This project showed me how data can uncover hidden patterns that help organizations better understand and support their people.

portfolio.title: Rest Assured: The SQL Side of Sleep Quality
portfolio.description: In this project, I explored the deep and often overlooked connection between our daily habits and the quality of our sleep—a topic that hit close to home as someone who struggles with rest myself. What began as a personal curiosity quickly turned into a meaningful analysis of how factors like weight, stress levels, and even occupation influence how well we sleep. Using real health and lifestyle data, I uncovered some surprising patterns—like the fact that engineers tend to sleep better regardless of their activity levels, and that lower stress consistently leads to better rest. This project gave me not just insights, but also a better understanding of my own sleep habits and how to improve them.
